node.title: Re: How to get better exponentiation?
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I don’t know if C’s pow(3) function has the same limitations under Unix?

Yes, I get NaN on Linux too, and [man://pow;3|pow(3)] says "The functions pow(x, y), powf(x, y), and powl(x, y) raise an invalid exception and return an NaN if x < 0 and y is not an integer." and similarly, on my system the manpage says "If x is a finite value less than 0, and y is a finite noninteger, a domain error occurs, and a NaN is returned." If you [https://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?i=(-8)^(1/3)|ask Wolfram Alpha], you have to explicitly tell it you want the real-valued root instead of the principal root, though I'm not enough of an expert to know whether that's relevant here (I did find out you can get all the principal roots via [doc://Math::Complex]'s root). Interestingly, [doc://Math::BigInt] and [doc://Math::BigFloat]'s ->broot(3) also return NaN, so throwing a [doc://bignum|use bignum;] in the program unfortunately doesn't help in this case.

To get the cube root, you can apparently use [man://cbrt;3|cbrt(3)], exposed via [doc://POSIX] as of Perl v5.22:

$ perl -wMstrict -MPOSIX=cbrt -le 'print cbrt(-8)' -2
